title: REPORT on gender inequalities in health, specifically as regards gender-specific conditions
part_text: Text as a whole without the word: ‘mandatory’
part_context: Stresses that the lack of understanding of sex- and gender-based differences in health is exacerbated by the fact that the data outcomes of research are rarely disaggregated by sex and gender; calls on the Commission to make the collection and reporting of sex- and gender-disaggregated data <del>mandatory</del> in all EU-funded projects so as to ensure accountability and the effective use of public resources; notes that AI could be used to identify sex or gender biases in existing or historical research to prevent the need to repeat the research; warns, however, that the use of AI must be monitored closely to ensure that it does not impose biases;
